statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commercial One-Stop Online Application System - https://onestop.nat.gov.tw
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English name may be recorded only as an auxiliary name and does not satisfy the legal uniqueness requirement. Latin/Pinyin transliteration is acceptable for cross-reference purposes but cannot be the primary registered name; all foreign corporate names must be translated and transliterated consistently in the registration filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The MOEA company name and business scope pre-approval is valid for 180 days and may be extended for one further 180-day period upon justified application. If rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days under the Administrative Appeal Act. A subsequent administrative action may be filed with the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months. For practical speed, the applicant may also file a new name pre-approval application with alternative names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and mail-forwarding-only addresses are not permissible for a licensed money transmission entity. The Taiwan entity must maintain a physical, accessible registered office in Taiwan with personnel resident for AML/CFT compliance and record-keeping. A serviced business center may be used only if it provides a dedicated private office staffed during business hours and is acceptable to the MOEA and FSC; pure virtual office addresses will not satisfy commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - estimated 80% annual likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspection for licensed remittance operators. The FSC and the Central Bank of Taiwan also require a mandatory pre-license on-site examination of the proposed registered office before issuing the remittance license.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Taiwan Company Act post-2018 amendment; however, for a licensed cross-border remittance agency, the Financial Supervisory Commission requires a minimum paid-in capital of NT$20,000,000 with full deposit in a dedicated escrow account at a domestic bank, subject to FSC verification and pre-licensing capital lock

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit online application for proposed Chinese and English company names and business scope 'Cross-Border Money Transmission Services (ISIC 6619)' using the MOEACA e-government interface; attach identification of shareholders and proposed director; pay NT$600 fee electronically; receive name and scope approval letter valid for six months. step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, adjust the trade name with transliteration or add a differentiating prefix/suffix and resubmit within 14 days; file administrative protest with MOEACA for unlawful rejection within 30 days of receipt of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company capital escrow account in the proposed company name with a Taiwan bank; have all shareholders remit paid-in capital via telegraphic transfer or domestic remittance; obtain a deposit certificate; CPA issues a capital verification report (查核報告書) after verifying the escrow balance, ensuring no withdrawal prior to completion of FSC licensing capital-lock requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or CPA queries the origin of funds, submit Anti-Money-Laundering source-of-funds declarations, shareholders' bank statements, and underlying business contracts to clarify and satisfy bank due diligence; amend subscription records if there is a discrepancy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (Company Registration Online System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application electronically with notarized article of incorporation and shareholder/officer consent; attach the CPA capital verification report, registered office lease or ownership proof, and director/shareholder identification; pay NTD 1,000 plus signaling fee based on authorized capital; after approval, receive the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書). step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEACA issues a query or deficiency notice, respond through the online rectification portal within 15 days; attorney rewrite or supplement notarization; failure to cure after 30 days triggers re-filing; Court appeal under Company Act Article 394 for unreasonable rejection.

required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease or ownership documents
Identity documents of responsible person (Chairperson)
Application for Business Tax Registration and Uniform Invoices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax authority requests clarifications on cross-border transaction scope, provide the FSC business plan, targeted payment rail agreements, and service liability insurance; appeal internal review within 30 days of unfavorable tax registration decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Licensing and FSC Money Transmission Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau; and Money Laundering Control Act registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a separate license application with FSC under the Banking Act and Regulations on Money Laundering Prevention for Cross-Border Remittance Agencies; submit incorporation certificate, capital escrow evidence, business program, AML/CFT internal controls, designated compliance officer, officer background checks, and fidelity bond evidence; obtain FSC business permit prior to commencing operational remittance services. Also register as an MSB (Money Services Business) with FSC under Article 13 of the Money Laundering Control Act.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Capital escrow certificate and CPA verification
Two-year business plan for cross-border remittance rails
AML/CFT policies, risk assessment, and transaction monitoring procedure
Designation of AML Compliance Officer and internal reporting channel
Fidelity bond or insured guarantee certificate
Employees' identification and criminal background declarations
Service provider agreements for Swift and local cash pickup clearing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FSC issues corrective queries or rejects, submit supplementary documents within the specified grace period; engage an external AML auditor to remediate control gaps; request in-person FSC meeting; judicial review under Administrative Litigation Act if license is unlawfully denied.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (formerly Environmental Protection Administration), Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal Environmental Impact Assessment; office-based business activity under Service Industry Category B, with no wastewater discharge, no industrial production process, and no hazardous material handling; if data center addition is made, Class C registration may apply
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge; indoor air quality complies with Article 6 of Indoor Air Quality Management Act, including carbon dioxide below 1,000 ppm and formaldehyde below 0.08 ppm; general waste handled under Waste Disposal Act Article 15; electronic records must follow data security not environmental discharge limits

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire safety certification from the local City Fire Bureau before occupancy, including fire prevention equipment inspection and evacuation plan approval; structural load inspection certificate from a licensed civil/structural engineer for office floor loading supporting 24/7 payment servers; occupational safety clearance under Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA, Taiwan) for safe electrical wiring and ergonomic workplace; fire drill records and emergency lighting certification must be retained on premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; official e-Tax filing portal: https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn. Where a Taiwan permanent establishment is separately established, the Taiwan tax authority is the Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw; CN_JV_LTD is primarily registered in China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: CN_JV_LTD, as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, obtains a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation upon incorporation; this USCC is the statutory tax identification number. Within 30 days after issuance of the business license, the joint venture must complete tax registration with the local STA office or through the e-Tax portal by submitting the articles of association, incorporation certificate, registered address proof, bank account confirmation, and capital contribution schedule. A foreign enterprise not established in China may receive a temporary tax identification number from the local STA for withholding and VAT purposes using its home-country TIN, certificate of incorporation, and relevant contract documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. CN_JV_LTD is a limited liability resident enterprise for PRC Corporate Income Tax (CIT) purposes, taxed on worldwide income at the statutory rate of 25%. It is not a pass-through entity and does not qualify for flow-through or transparent treatment under PRC tax law. Non-resident branches or Taiwan-source income would be brought into the CIT net through the ordinary resident-enterprise framework, subject to bilateral treaty and anti-deferral rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: PRC law does not provide a US-style check-the-box or general entity classification election; tax classification is statutorily determined. Available elections include: (1) the VAT general taxpayer election, with compulsory general taxpayer status where annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; (2) for qualifying cross-border taxable services, the election between VAT zero-rating with input credit and VAT exemption without input credit; (3) CIT preferential elections, such as the 15% reduced rate for qualifying Advanced Technology or Advanced Technology Service Enterprises; and (4) fixed-ratio or actual-flow methodologies under transfer-pricing documentation. No hybrid mismatch election exists; PRC anti-hybrid rules in CIT Law Article 46 and the Special Tax Adjustments regime apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Law; financial and payment services are taxed at 6%, while the general standard rate on goods is 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for VAT identity; every taxpayer must register on establishment. Compulsory general VAT taxpayer registration applies where annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. Small-scale taxpayers may elect general taxpayer status, and cross-border zero-rating claims ordinarily require general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices, including zero-rated export service invoices, must be issued through the STA electronic invoice platform integrated with the Golden Tax Phase IV system. Fully digitalized electronic invoices (全电发票) are generated with a unique blockchain-backed invoice code, transmitted in real time to the e-Tax platform, and cleared through automated fiscal authentication. No physical tax stamp is required; issuance is legally effective only after digital clearance, and API-based line-item matching reconciles invoice data against VAT returns and cross-border payment evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under CaiShui [2016] 36 and SAT Notice 2016 No. 29, zero VAT rating is available for cross-border taxable services supplied by a PRC VAT general taxpayer where: (1) the service is provided to an overseas entity or individual; (2) the service is consumed entirely outside the PRC; (3) the consideration is received from overseas and settled in foreign currency or through offshore RMB accounts; and (4) the taxpayer maintains contemporaneous evidence of overseas consumption. For remittance services, zero-rating applies only where the service recipient is outside the PRC and the payment transmission service is wholly performed outside China. If any local cash-pickup or domestic settlement leg occurs in China, that portion is generally treated as domestic VATable service at 6% rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: PRC Customs Export Declaration (出口报关单) — required where tangible ancillary goods are exported; not applicable to pure remittance services
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill — required for any associated cargo movement
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt Voucher (收汇核销单) issued by the settlement bank
Cross-Border Service Trade Contract and ICA/EFT evidence identifying the overseas service recipient and scope of services
VAT zero-rated export service filing and proof of overseas consumption, including the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation or tax registration
Foreign exchange declaration in the SAFE trade-in-services monitoring system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Improper or fraudulent zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective clawback of the uncollected output VAT, daily surcharges at 0.05% of the arrears, administrative fines of up to five times the tax evaded, and criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Article 204 for fraudulent export VAT refunds where the amount exceeds RMB 50,000. The STA matches export service contracts, foreign exchange receipt data, and invoice records through Golden Tax Phase IV; late repatriation beyond the 180-day benchmark may trigger denial of zero-rating, with reassessment and clawback of any previously claimed input VAT credit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (中国人民银行, PBOC); exchange-control administration is delegated to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (国家外汇管理局, SAFE). CN_JV_LTD is a mainland-China Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, so the PRC PBOC/SAFE regulatory regime governs all treasury, capital-account, and payment-rail matters. The Taiwan-headquartered shareholder enjoys no exemption from SAFE filing, bank designation, or transaction coding requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is fully convertible for current-account items (trade in goods and services, dividends, interest, royalties, and salaries) under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations (State Council Order No. 532). Capital-account items - equity paid-in capital, inward shareholder loans, equity transfers, and liquidation proceeds - are only conditionally convertible and require SAFE registration or approval before the receiving bank may credit funds. For this JV, a dividend remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is permitted on the current account without a separate quota provided: (1) the annual financial statements have been audited by an onshore licensed CPA; (2) statutory surplus reserves have been accrued under the Company Law; (3) all corporate income tax, VAT, and dividend withholding tax (10% standard, or a reduced cross-strait treaty rate, generally 5%, where the Taiwan ultimate beneficial-owner certificate is accepted) have been settled; and (4) the outward amount is not disguising capital-account flows such as repayment of intercompany loans or advance repatriation of paid-in capital. Key remaining hurdle: the JV's ISIC 6619 activity is a regulated cross-border payment service; SAFE taxes client-fund flows and the JV's own commission income under separate classifications, and the JV may not treat client float as treasury liquidity. Liquidation and equity repatriation additionally require a capital-account registration and a tax-clearing certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory percentage surrender of export proceeds to the central bank in the PRC; the former surrender requirement has been abolished. However, SAFE still applies the repatriation and verification rules of the goods- and services-trade regimes. The JV's commission income derived from overseas agents and sponsors is treated as service-export proceeds that must be repatriated onshore into a domestic foreign-exchange or RMB settlement account; offshore retention is permitted only under an approved closed-end cash-pool arrangement. SAFE's trade-classification system designates the firm as A/B/C class: an A-class firm settles and verifies receipts without per-transaction limits, whereas B-class and C-class firms must register each collection and may be obliged by the bank to repatriate and settle within 60 days and 30 days, respectively. For the remittance-agency line of business, client funds are not export proceeds at all: PBOC and SAFE require instruction-by-instruction matching of collected RMB against each customer's payout, daily position settlement, and zero proprietary use of client float. The JV's own service-revenue component may be retained in foreign currency or settled into RMB at the JV's discretion, subject to the A/B/C classification and the bank's post-transaction verification window.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW / effectively unavailable for direct onboarding. A foreign digital EMI (including Taiwan-based payment firms, Wise/Airwallex-style platforms, and other non-bank electronic money institutions) cannot independently maintain a RMB settlement account, client-funds account, or SAFE capital account in mainland China unless it has obtained the PBOC non-bank payment institution licence under the Regulation on the Supervision and Administration of Non-bank Payment Institutions (effective May 2024) and SAFE cross-border payment registration. There is no EU/UK-style EMI passporting for a Taiwan or Hong Kong entity in the PRC. Therefore the JV must operate through its own licensed mainland bank accounts, or, at most, use an overseas EMI as a technology-only front-end that routes cleared funds to a mainland-licensed payment institution. Any design in which the offshore EMI holds or commingles settlement funds for PRC-destination customers is a regulatory hardening failure and will be rejected by the clearing bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence is effectively mandated. PBOC corporate-account-opening rules and the anti-money laundering KYC framework require the mainland legal representative (or the sole authorised senior manager under a board resolution plus the legal representative's personal identity evidence and video confirmation) to appear in person at the account-maintaining branch for a recorded compliance interview. The Taiwan-appointed director cannot substitute the mainland legal representative; the bank accepts the Taiwan shareholder only as a beneficial owner subject to enhanced due diligence, requiring notarised corporate documents from Taiwan (or the cross-strait notarisation protocol), passport copies of the ultimate owners, and an ownership-chain diagram. Remote-only opening is not offered in practice to an ISIC 6619 money-transmission counterparty; even under the 2018 corporate account-opening reform package, the first activation and the final compliance interview are completed physically at the branch. Some Tier-1 banks will additionally request the JV's compliance officer to attend the interview when the client is classified as a high-risk money-service business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Money-service-business classification - the JV's ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522390 activity is auto-tiered high-risk and triggers enhanced due diligence at every Tier-1 bank; without a statutory licence the account application will be declined by the bank's AML engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PBOC cross-border remittance payment business licence or filing certificate; SAFE approval or registration for payment-institution foreign-exchange business; the JV's AML internal-control manual; suspicious-transaction reporting procedures (STR) referencing PBOC Order No. 3; a signed compliance-officer declaration; organisation chart showing the licensed compliance officer; details of segregated client-funds accounts with the designated custodian bank; annual independent audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity - a Taiwan corporate shareholder behind a mainland JV creates a red flag if the individual ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more cannot be verified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register naming every natural person holding 25% or more; a chain-of-control diagram from the Taiwan parent to the individual UBOs; notarised board resolutions; passport copies and proof-of-residence for each UBO; adverse-media and sanctions-screening reports; the Taiwan parent's audited financial statements; a bank reference letter from a reputable Taiwan correspondent; source-of-wealth narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-velocity anomaly - the bank's monitoring profile suspects that a high-volume, small-value consumer-remittance rail is being used for underground banking or illegal gambling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE/PBOC-approved transaction-purpose mapping; per-customer annual transmission caps and daily volume limits; the JV's customer due-diligence policy including source-of-funds evidence rules for cash pickup; real-time transaction monitoring with blockchain-analytics vendor reports; agreed suspicious-transaction thresholds; daily escrow balance certificates issued to the clearing bank; an independent AML audit confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and cross-strait legal ambiguity - SWIFT name-screening may hit 'Taiwan, China' country descriptors and the correspondent network may decline flows to Taiwan-domiciled payees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual proof that no remittance is routed for persons or entities in comprehensively-sanctioned jurisdictions; the JV's SWIFT BIC/LEI registry profile; OFAC/EU/UN list-clearing logs; a country and currency policy confirming that TWD and RMB may only clear to legitimate licensed banks in Taiwan; FATF Recommendation 16 payment transparency data (full payer and beneficiary names embedded in every wire); an internal policy prohibiting shell-company counterparties and unlicensed money transmitters.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Injection from the Taiwan parent to the mainland JV is made exclusively by SWIFT MT103 credit to the JV's SAFE-designated capital account (资本金账户). Prior to any wire, the JV must complete the Foreign-Investment Information Report and obtain the bank-side FDI registration reference. The outward instruction from the Taiwan shareholder must state its purpose as 'equity investment - capital contribution to a foreign-invested enterprise' and must carry the BOP direct-investment transaction code published by SAFE for that purpose; the numeric code is displayed by the receiving bank's foreign-exchange system at the point of registration because SAFE updates the coding list in its periodic reporting circulars. Funds must be remitted from the shareholder's own corporate bank account; cash, third-party-funded, or commingled instructions are rejected by the receiving compliance system. After the capital account has been credited, the JV may settle the proceeds into RMB within two business days or retain the foreign currency, subject to the negative-list restrictions. Paid-in capital must be recorded at the historical spot rate, disclosed in the annual information report, and supported by the industrial and commercial receipt voucher and the board resolution. Any subsequent return or withdrawal of equity capital requires a separate SAFE capital-account registration and liquidation/tax clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The JV uses tiered clearing rails as follows: (1) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for commissions, dividend remittances, and customer payouts to overseas beneficiaries; (2) SWIFT MT202/MT202COV bank-to-bank cover where the beneficiary bank is not directly connected; (3) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 through the MT700/MT707 series, funded at maturity by MT103/MT202; (4) for cross-border RMB, the mandatory rail is CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System); where the counterparty bank is in Taiwan, settlement may alternatively clear through the Taiwan RMB clearing arrangement operated by Bank of China (Taipei branch); (5) for domestic last-mile cash pickup, the JV batched client-payout files over CNAPS/IBPS to the local agent network, with the overseas portion transmitted via SWIFT gpi to the paying agent. Every outbound payment must be accompanied by the underlying contract, invoice, and SAFE-compliant purpose code; dividend and profit outflows additionally require the tax-payment vouchers and the audited financial certificate; trade-related disbursements must be matched in the bank's post-transaction surveillance system against the customs declaration or the service-trade transaction certificate within the prescribed verification window.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY forward (远期结售汇) - permitted only for genuine current-account or capital-account exposure and executed with the designated FX bank under SAFE's real-demand principle
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (货币掉期) - permitted to hedge long-term USD/TWD/RMB debt and investment cash flows
FX swaps (外汇掉期) - permitted for short-term liquidity and rollover management
Plain-vanilla FX options (汇率期权) - permitted for hedging purposes, generally on a bought-option basis; sold-option or structured strategies require documented hedging rationale

Offshore RMB deliverable forwards (CNH forwards) - not permitted as onshore instruments for the JV; onshore RMB non-deliverable-forward (NDF) trades are prohibited, so any CNH hedge must be executed offshore through the Taiwan parent's treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting and Resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened by 30 June of the following fiscal year; minutes recorded and kept at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene within the statutory period subjects responsible persons to a MOEA-imposed fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000; continued non-compliance may lead to an administrative order convening the meeting and, ultimately, forced dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Business Operation Report, and Profit Appropriation/Loss Coverage Plan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved by the ordinary shareholders' meeting not later than 30 June; MOEA filing is due within 15 days after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing of audited financial statements may result in a MOEA fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 per occurrence; intentionally false statements may trigger criminal liability under the Company Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and Settlement Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (local tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May of the year following the taxable year for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and payment attract a monthly delinquency surcharge of 3% of unpaid tax, up to a maximum of 10%; where no return is filed, the tax authority makes an official assessment and may impose additional fines on the responsible person. Prolonged non-payment may result in enforced tax collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Self-Assessment and Operations Report (licensed remittance institution filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for calendar-year institutions, ordinarily by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or deficient AML/CFT filings may draw fines under the Money Laundering Control Act ranging from NT$500,000 to NT$10,000,000 per violation; severe or repeated breaches can result in license revocation and closure of the remittance franchise.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Report (for the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the close of the fiscal year; e.g., by the end of February for a calendar-year entity, unless the approval letter stipulates another date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign investment report may result in administrative fines, suspension of investment incentives and foreign exchange repatriation privileges, or an order to rectify; continued default may jeopardize the validity of the foreign investment approval.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit for all licensed remittance and payment institutions regardless of paid-in capital; for non-regulated companies, audit is mandatory when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million, for financial businesses, or when directed by MOEA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS) as endorsed by the FSC applies to regulated financial and payment institutions; non-regulated non-public companies may apply ROC GAAP, but the company must apply the same framework consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: As a licensed remittance agency, the company must maintain current registers of shareholders, directors, supervisors, and actual beneficial owners. Beneficial ownership must be re-confirmed at least annually within the AML/CFT risk assessment; any share transfer or control change requires updating statutory registers and, for foreign shareholding changes, prior notification to and approval by the MOEA Investment Commission where required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book for board and shareholders' meetings
Accounting books, ledgers, and financial statement copies

stage_6.infraction_category: Area of violation (e.g. Tax Evasion, Shell Company, AML)
stage_6.statutory_sanction: Specific legal sanction and financial penalty
stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment
